title: Free homotopy classes of loops are conjugacy classes
statement: Let $X$ be a path-connected topological space with basepoint $x_0$. Two loops at $x_0$ are freely homotopic if and only if the corresponding elements of $\pi_1(X,x_0)$ are conjugate; consequently free homotopy classes of loops in $X$ correspond bijectively to conjugacy classes in $\pi_1(X,x_0)$.
strategy: A free homotopy $H\colon S^1\times I\to X$ between loops $\alpha,\beta$ gives, after choosing the path $t\mapsto H(1,t)$, the conjugation relation in the fundamental group (standard rearrangement of the cylinder decomposition of $S^1\times I$); conversely a conjugation $\beta=\gamma\alpha\gamma^{-1}$ is realized by a free homotopy that first transports the basepoint along $\gamma$ and then back. The group laws and well-definedness of $[\gamma][\alpha][\gamma]^{-1}$ are the published fundamental-group laws.

references.title: Ozsvath, Stipsicz and Szabo, Grid Homology for Knots and Links, AMS Surveys and Monographs 208 (2015); section 2.1 and Appendix B.1, printed pp. 367-372
